claims.statement: For every finite ordinary connected tree T, with integer p=alpha(T)-2 and x(T) the least natural index for which Delta_x(T)<0, x(T)+2<=p implies alpha(T)>=7.
claims.scope: Exact auxiliary eligibility guard on finite ordinary connected trees, with the first strict descent and integer p fixed by SEMANTIC-CONTRACT.md; no residuality premise.
claims.reason: The r27 arbitrary-rank forest descent bound gives n<=4x at k=x. Eligibility and alpha<n force the contrary case alpha<=6 to have alpha=6, x=2, and n in {7,8}; exact tree coefficient formulas plus the one- and two-vertex cover degree bounds give Delta_2>0 in both cases, contradiction.

limitations: This proves only the auxiliary eligibility guard; the proposed tagged-shadow inequality and the primary complete favorable-leaf aggregate remain open.
The exact Prüfer-code enumeration covers labeled trees only at orders seven and eight and is corroborative finite evidence, not the universal proof.
The fresh K_{1,10} example is a boundary consistency check for the proposed tail mechanism and does not prove its general inequality.
